content.title: A look at Texas women’s basketball head coach Vic Schaefer
content.text: Head coach Vic Schaefer talks with his team after the Longhorns beat Alabama in the second round of the March Madness tournament. Sunday, March 24, 2024. The 2024-25 season marked the inaugural season for the Texas Longhorns and Oklahoma Sooners joining the SEC. The Lady Vols already had their first test at home against the Sooners, losing a close 87-86 contest. Now all eyes turn to Tennessee’s first matchup against the Texas Longhorns, led by head coach Vic Schaefer. The 2024-25 season marks Schaefer’s fifth season with the program, and the five years have been quite kind to Schaefer. He has compiled a record of 109-32 during his first four years at the University of Texas and was named Big 12 Coach of the Year in 2023. Schaefer was formally named head coach on March 13, 2012, by the Mississippi State Bulldogs of the ladies basketball team. The Schaefer-led Bulldogs reached the NCAA postseason five times in his eight seasons, and were well in line to reach the tournament in Schaefer’s 2020 season with the team. The team was also ranked No. 3 in preseason rankings when Schaefer departed. “I’m walking away from what’s already been ranked as the preseason No. 3 team in the country,” Schaefer said after joining the Longhorns. “But again, it comes back to a calling, an opportunity you just can’t walk away from.” Schaefer had called the state of Texas home before. He was hired as an associate head coach for Texas A&M for nine seasons prior to taking the reins at Mississippi State. The highlight of Schaefer’s time in Starkville was making two consecutive national championship games. In 2017, his Bulldogs beat Connecticut in overtime in the semifinals to advance before losing to South Carolina. A year later, Mississippi State needed overtime to advance again, defeating Louisville, before Arike Ogunbowale’s last-second basket won the national championship for Notre Dame. Schaefer’s stint with Mississippi State ended in 2020. Due to COVID-19, he didn’t lead the Bulldogs on a final NCAA Tournament run. Since taking over the Longhorns, Schaefer has continued to cement his name as one of the top coaches in women’s basketball. The veteran coach has been to the Elite Eight three times in his first four years in Austin. Schaefer’s fifth season with the Longhorns is off to an impressive start. Texas holds a record of 18-2 and is ranked No. 7 in the AP poll. The Longhorns enter Thursday’s contest with Tennessee off a blowout win over No. 8 Maryland on Monday. Still, Schaefer recognizes the challenge of taking on the Lady Vols. “We’ve got our work cut out for us, no question about it,” Schaefer said. “I mean, I can’t remember the last time I’ve gotten ready for a conference opponent who in conference only is averaging almost 86 points a game. That is a prolific offensive team. They’re going to play, you know, 10, 11 kids, they’re going to challenge you.” Schaefer’s defensive-minded approach is a counter the Longhorns are going to fall back on against an aggressive offensive Lady Vol attack. This season, the Longhorns have shined defensively, allowing just 55.4 points per game. “I don’t think we’re going to go out and shut them down, hold them to 50 points,” Schaefer said. “They’re just too good, you know. But we’ve done a good job all year, for the most part, of taking away the three-point line with certain opponents. And you know, this team will be no different.” About the Contributor
